sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the world's stability depends specifically on the three things (Torah, service, and acts of kindness) because they reveal that the inner purpose of the world itself is to manifest G-dliness.

translations.translation: Based on this, we can explain the statement, "The world stands on three things,"
for this implies
that for the world to have stability
(the revelation of G-dliness in the world),
it is not only the general matter of Torah and mitzvos that is relevant,
but specifically the matter of the three things,
for the concept of the world's stability is
that the revelation of G-dliness drawn into the world through Torah and mitzvos should not be like an added thing,
but rather that it be revealed that the intention and inner essence of the world
(the concealment)
itself is that there should be a revelation of G-dliness within it,
and this matter within Torah and mitzvos is through their division into three things
(three categories),
Torah, service [prayer], and acts of kindness.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of Ein Sof—the descending light that fills worlds and the transcendent encompassing light—correspond to the two dynamics of "above" and "below" found in all worlds.

translations.translation: B)
This will be understood by prefacing what was explained above
(in the previous maamar)
in the explanation of the Sages' statement,
"The light of Ein Sof is above, above, without end, and below, below, without limit,"
that "above" and "below" are
(generally speaking)
Atzilus and BY"A [Beri'ah, Yetzirah, Asiyah],
and the meaning of "the light of Ein Sof is above... and below..." is
that the superiority and perfection of the light of Ein Sof is in two matters:
In the matter of the drawing down and descent below to bring into being and vitalize the creations of BY"A,
and within this itself—"below, below, without limit,"
that it is drawn down to vitalize the creations of this physical world, beneath which there is no lower level,
and even to the extent that it is drawn down to vitalize even the kelipos,
and in the matter of loftiness,
that even the highest worlds,
Atzilus and above Atzilus,
"above, above,"
their coming into being is from only an illumination,
which is incomparable relative to His essence.
These two matters are
(generally speaking)
the Or HaMemaleh [the Immanent Light] and the Or HaSovev [the Transcendent Light].
For in the Or HaMemaleh is the matter of descent and drawing down below to vitalize creations according to their level,
and in the Or HaSovev is the matter of transcendence and loftiness,
that all the worlds
(and also the light that is enclothed within them)
are incomparable and considered as nothing relative to His essence.
And from these two matters in the light of Ein Sof, the two matters of "above" and "below" are made in the worlds.
For the matter of "above" and "below" exists in all worlds.
The existence of the worlds
(even the existence in Atzilus and above Atzilus)
is the "below" within them,
and the matter of ratzo [running/striving upward],
the exit from existence
(which exists in all worlds,
even in BY"A)
is the "above" within them.
And these two matters in the worlds derive from the two aforementioned matters in the light of Ein Sof.
For from the Or HaMemaleh, which is in a movement of descent and drawing down below,
is made the "below"
(the existence)
in the worlds,
and the "above" in the worlds
(the ratzo within them, in which they strive to exit their existence)
is from the revelation of the loftiness of the light of Ein Sof
(Sovev).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of Ein Sof—descent and ascent—are for the sake of their parallel in human service: Torah (drawing down) and prayer (elevating), with Torah's descent reaching even the lowest states.

translations.translation: C)
Now, it is known
that creation is for the sake of man,
the intention of this is not only for the creation of the worlds
(including even the world of Atzilus and the worlds of Ein Sof above Atzilus),
but for all revelations,
even the most sublime revelations.
Based on this, it can be said
that the intention of the two aforementioned matters in the light of Ein Sof—
the matter of the descent and drawing down below of the Or HaMemaleh and the matter of the elevation and loftiness of the Or HaSovev—
including also the root of these two matters as they are in the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum
[the light of the ascent of the will, which is the root of the Or HaMemaleh, and the light that precedes the ascent of the will, which is the root of the Or HaSovev],
is
so that there should be
(analogous)
these two matters in the service of man.
In general, they are the two lines of Torah and prayer.
For prayer is an elevation from below to above,
for through the contemplation of prayer, one exits his existence, to the point of coming to divestment from physicality.
And Torah is a drawing down from above to below.
For the matter of engaging in Torah is
(not that a person nullifies his intellect,
but rather, on the contrary),
that the Torah is drawn down and enclothed in the intellect of the person,
a drawing down from above to below.
And furthermore,
the drawing down of Torah
(which is drawn down into the intellect of the person)
occurs even when the person is in a state opposite to purity,
similar to the matter of the light of Ein Sof "below, below, without limit,"
which is drawn down to vitalize not only the creations of this physical world but even the kelipos.
And just as in the matter of "below, below, without limit,"
even when it is drawn down below to vitalize the creations and even the kelipos,
the light is not changed by this,
so too is it with the drawing down of Torah,
that even as it is drawn down into the intellect of the person,
and even when the person is in a state opposite to purity,
it is the word of G-d.
